text: On the BoolQ testbed, we evaluated a weak-to-strong generalization method that discards training examples where weak supervisors disagree, using a minimum agreement threshold of 0.8. Across 16 seeds, the method attained a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.67 with a standard error of 0.12. No baseline PGR was supplied in this experiment's data, so we cannot characterize this figure as an improvement over, or a regression from, naive weak supervision or any alternative filtering scheme; the number should be read only as the absolute level of gap recovery achieved under this configuration. The standard error of 0.12 indicates non-trivial seed-to-seed spread, so the underlying effect could plausibly be somewhat higher or lower than the point estimate. Results are specific to BoolQ and to the 0.8 agreement threshold, and no sweep over thresholds or additional datasets is reported here, so generalization to other tasks or stricter and looser filtering levels remains untested.
